Brief facts of the case Late T. Velayudhan, is the father of the plaintiff and the father-in-law of the Defendant Nos. 1 and 4. Said T. Velayudhan married Smt. Kanthamma and within their wedlock they had three children namely, the plaintiff, husband of defendant No.1, Venkatesh V. and the husband of defendant No.4 namely, V. Dorai Kanna.The defendant 2 & 3 are the minor children of Late Venkatesh V. The plaintiff and defendants constitute a undivided Hindu Joint family of Late Velayudhan and are governed by the provisions of the Mithakshara School of Law. During the lifetime of said Velayudhan he had inherited certain property from his ancestors in property bearing Survey Nos. 67 sub Division No. 2M-30 cents, Survey Nos. 67 sub Division No. 2H-70 cents, Survey Nos. 68 sub Division No. 10-40 cents, and in Survey Nos. 68 sub Division No. 13-40 cents, in all measuring 180 cents, situated at Madhandakuppam Village, Katpadi Town Taluk, Vellore C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 District, Tamil Nadu, described as Item No. 1 of the suit schedule property. It is the further case of the plaintiff that item No.2 of the suit schedule property was purchased by Sri Velayudhan under the registered Sale Deed, dated 23.10.1974, from one Sri MK Puttabuddi son of Kullappa and later the said property was again conveyed by the BDA to the Plaintiff's father under a registered Sale Deed dated 28.03.1983. while item No.3 was purchased by the mother Smt. Kanthamma under the Sale Deed, dated 13.12.1971. According to the plaintiff Smt. Kanthamma had expressed her intention to give away item No.3 of the suit schedule property to the plaintiff as Sthreedhana property. However, Smt. Kanthamma died intestate without executing any instrument in favour of the plaintiff.

Meanwhile the father of the plaintiff after the death of his wife Smt. Kanthamma without the knowledge and consent of the plaintiff got item No.3 of the property transferred in his name. It is averred C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 that the BDA had also executed Transfer Agreement in favour of Sri Velayudhan. In this manner Sri Velayudhan has acquired title to item No.1 to 3 of the schedule properties. It is further submitted by the plaintiff that somewhere in 2003 Sri Velayudhan did not have funds to develop the property and therefore, he had requested the husband of the plaintiff to add his own costs with an understanding that he may use the property for his exclusive benefit in future. Relying on the representation of Sri Velayudhan, the husband of the plaintiff invested his hard earned money and constructed two floors with two bed room house and after completion of construction the father of the plaintiff mutually divided the property by giving ground floor to Venkatesh, first floor to Dorai Kannan and 2 nd floor to the plaintiff. Hence, from the said date they are in the Mahalakshmi V Alias Baby vs Sangeetha on 27 March, 2026 separate possession of their respective shares. C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 On 02.10.2019 Sri Venkatesh died leaving behind the defendants No.1 to 3 while on 22.05.2015 Dorai Kannan died leaving behind the defendant No.4. According to the plaintiff, the defendant No.4 had filed O.S.No. 2375/2017 seeking eviction of the husband of the defendant No.1. Meanwhile the plaintiff intervened and advised the defendant No.4 to withdraw the suit by intimating her to affect partition in the joint family properties.

The defendant No.4 though agreed to withdraw the suit and affect partition, but surprisingly instituted the suit in O.S.No. 647/2019 against the plaintiff and defendants No.1 to 3 for the relief of declaration and possession by claiming her right on the basis of the alleged Will dated 10.11.2010. Initially the defendant No.4 had agreed to withdraw the suit and affect partition, but later on she refused to withdraw the suit and therefore, the plaintiff has approached this court. C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 According to the plaintiff, the Will executed by Sri Velayudhan is without any absolute title over item No.1 as it was purchased out of nucleus of the joint family. The alleged Will executed by Sri Velayudhan is a fabricated document by defendant No.4 and as such it is not binding on the plaintiff. Under the Will item No.2 is bequeathed to Sri Dorai Kannan and item No.3 is bequeathed to Sri Venkatesh. It is averred that Item No.3 was acquired by mother of the plaintiff and after her death, Sri Velayudhan had obtained Transfer Agreement from BDA. The plain reading of the Transfer Agreement would reveal that item No.3 is the self acquired property of Smt. Kanthamma and same was inherited by Sri Velayudhan by way of succession. The Will executed by Sri Velayudhan is shrouded with suspicious circumstances as Sri Velayudhan was aged, sick and infirm at the time of execution of the Will. Thus, neither the defendant No.4 nor the defendants No.1 to 3 derive any independent title over C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 the properties bequeathed under the Will. Thus, the said Will was obtained by playing fraud on the plaintiff. In fact, the husband of the defendant No.1 namely Sri Venkatesh had denied the alleged Will when he was contesting the suit filed by the defendant No.4.

Now, only with an intention to deprive the legitimate right of the plaintiff, the husband of the defendant No.4 has created the alleged Will. Thus, sought to decree the suit. MS. BHARGAVI, Daughter of late Venkatesh V, aged about 10 years, Defendant Nos. 2 & 3 being minors And represented by their mother And natural guardian Smt. Sangeetha. 4 O.S. In response to the suit summons, the defendants appeared through their counsel.the defendant No.1 has filed common written-statement on behalf of defendants No.2 & 3 by admitting the relationship between the parties and the mode of acquisition of the suit schedule properties. However, the defendant No.1has taken the following contentions. There was a family arrangement prior to the execution of the registered Will under which item No.1 was allotted to the husband of the defendant No.1 and C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 therefore, the plaintiff is not entitled to item No.1. Item No.2 of the suit schedule property was purchased by the father of the plaintiff and hence, it is the self acquired property of the father of the plaintiff. similarly, item No.3 was purchased out of the income of the father of the plaintiff in the name of his wife Smt. Kanthamma, who was only a housewife and had no independent source of income. After the death of Smt. Kanthamma, Sri Velayudhan acquired title over item No.3 as per the own admission of the plaintiff. Hence, the contention of the plaintiff that item No.3 is the self acquired property of Kantamma is incorrect. Sri Velayudhan was hale and healthy at the time of execution of the Will. After the demise of Sri Velayudhan, Venaktesh and Dorai Kannan, the defendants No.1 to 3 are in joint possession of item Mahalakshmi V Alias Baby vs Sangeetha on 27 March, 2026 No.1. The defendants No.1 to 3 have admitted the institution of O.S.No. 647/2019 by defendant No.4 against the defendants No.1 to 3. The defendants No.1 to 3 have C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 contended that another property bearing No.23 acquired by the father of the plaintiff in the name of Smt.

Kanthamma was given to the plaintiff under the registered release deed on 19.03.2009 and the plaintiff has suppressed about the execution of the registered release deed. The plaintiff has already been given her share in terms of the registered release deed and the said fact has already been disclosed in the Will dated 10.11.2011. Therefore, the plaintiff has no locus standi to challenge the Will. It is clearly stated in the Will that item No.1 of the suit property situated at Tamil Nadu is given to Venkatesh, the husband of the 1 st defendant and Dorai Kannan, the husband of 4 th defendant. Thus, the plaintiff is not entitled to any share in item No.1 of the schedule properties. It is further contended that the plaintiff has not incorporated the boundaries of item No.1 in the plaint and the said fact demonstrates that the plaintiff at no point of time was in joint possession and enjoyment of item No.1. It is further C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 averred that item No.3 of the suit schedule property has been bequeathed in favour of the husband of the defendant No.1 and he was in exclusive possession and enjoyment. After his demise, the defendants No.1 to 3 are in enjoyment of the same. Sri Velayudhan was a plumbing contractor and he was running his plumbing work in the name of M/s. Dorai Kannan Plumbing Works and out his self earnings, he had purchased item Nos.2 and 3 and also property bearing No.23, which is the subject matter of release deed. The father of the plaintiff was in sound disposing state of mind at the time of execution of the will deed and sought to dismiss the suit. The defendant No.4 has filed a separate written- statement admitting the relationship between the parties. She has also averred that property No.23 has been gifted by Sri Velayudhan to the plaintiff.

After the death of Smt. Kanthamma, Sri Velayudhan had no right to execute the gift deed in favour of the plaintiff in relation to the aforesaid C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 property. The plaintiff ought to have included the said property in the suit, but the plaintiff has not included it and hence, the suit is not maintainable. It is averred that Velayudhan had constructed and developed item No.2 of the property and therefore, the contention of the plaintiff that her husband developed item No.2 of the property is denied. The plaintiff and her husband are residing in a separate residence and therefore, the entire claim that she is residing in item No.2 of the suit schedule property is denied. When the husband of defendant No.1 started creating nuisance to defendant No.4 and also occupied item No.2 unauthorizedly, she filed a suit, which was withdrawn subsequently and now she has filed a suit for declaration and possession in respect of item No.2 in O.S.No. 647/2019. Neither the plaintiff nor the defendants No.1 to 3 have any right over item No.2 of the suit schedule property, since it is the self acquired property of Sri Velayudhan and it has been bequeathed to the husband of C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 defendant No.4. After the death of husband of defendant No.4, the defendant No.4 is the absolute owner and in possession of the said property. The defendant No.4 has obtained katha and other revenue records from BBMP and has obtained water and electricity connection. The plaintiff and her husband had no source of income and they were residing with the family of Sri Velayudhan and other defendants. Hence, sought to dismiss the suit.

MS. BHARGAVI, Daughter of late Venkatesh V, aged about 10 years, Defendant Nos. 2 & 3 being minors And represented by their mother And natural guardian Smt. Sangeetha. 4 O.S. The brief facts of the case in O.S.No. 647/2019, are as under: The plaintiff is owner of the suit schedule property bearing No.7, Old No. 842, 5th A cross Road, BSK 1 st Stage II block, Bengaluru consisting of ground floor, first and second floor. Originally the suit schedule property was owned by the father in law of the plaintiff Sri T. Velayudan son of Dondu Muniswamy Mudaliar and it was purchased from one Sri M.K. Puttabuddi, son of Kullappa under the registered sale deed dated 23.10.1974. Later on Sri T. Velayudan had got another sale deed from BDA on 28.03.1983. The father in law of the plaintiff had got the revenue documents transferred in his name and had got constructed ground floor plus two floors in the suit schedule property. During his lifetime he was in peaceful C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property. The father in law of the plaintiff had executed registered Will on 10.11.2010. As per the Will, the suit schedule property has been bequeathed in favour of Dorai Kannan, who is the husband of the plaintiff herein and another property was bequeathed in favour of defendant No.1 namely Sri Venkatesh. It is further contended that during the lifetime of Sri T. Velayudan he had gifted another property to defendant No.2 by way of gift deed. Sri T. Velayudan died on 11.11.2012 and the husband of the plaintiff died on 22.05.2015. After the death of the husband of the plaintiff, the plaintiff had obtained katha and revenue documents from BBMP in her name and has paid up to date taxes and also obtained water and BESCOM connection in her name.

During the lifetime of the father in law, the family of the plaintiff, defendants No.1 and 2 were residing in the suit schedule property, but after his demise, the husband of the plaintiff demanded the C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 defendants Mahalakshmi V Alias Baby vs Sangeetha on 27 March, 2026 No.1 and 2 to quit, vacate and deliver, which was in possession of the defendant No.1. It is further contended that the defendant No.1 occupied the ground floor portion excluding one room and the defendant No.2 occupied the 2nd floor portion of the suit schedule property. Now, the 2nd defendant has inducted a tenant in the 2 nd floor, who has arrayed as defendant No.3. It is further contended that the plaintiff is residing in the 1st floor including one room in the ground floor of the suit schedule property. During the lifetime of the husband of the plaintiff, he had requested the defendants No.1 and 2 to vacate, and hand over the possession of the suit property but they had requested for some more time, but even after the death of the husband of the plaintiff, they have failed to vacate the premises. The plaintiff had filed O.S.No. 2375/2017 against the defendant No.1 for the relief of injunction in respect of the suit schedule property. later on the said suit was withdrawn on 02.07.2018. Even C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 before institution of the said suit, she had requested the defendants on several occasions to handover the suit schedule property, but the defendants neglected and failed to vacate the suit schedule property. Hence, left with no other alternative, they have issued legal notice on 27.11.2018 calling upon the defendants to quit, vacate and handover the possession.

The said legal notice was duly served on the defendants and even after receipt of the notice, they failed to comply the demands made in the notice and hence, this suit. The plaintiff Smt. C. Lakshmi, wife of Late V. Dorai Kannan has filed the suit in O.S.No. 647/2019, who is the defendant NO.4 in O.S.No. 4177/2020 seeking the following reliefs: Mahalakshmi V Alias Baby vs Sangeetha on 27 March, 2026 i) To declare the plaintiff is the sole and absolute owner of the suit schedule property as per the Will dated 10-11-2010 Executed by the father in law of the plaintiff infavour of the husband of the plaintiff; C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 ii) To declare the Defendants are in unauthorized occupation of the suit schedule property and further to direct them to quit, vacate and hand over the vacant physical possession of the suit schedule property to the plaintiff; and iii) to grant Permanent Injunction restraining the defendants, their agents, servants, officials, contractors or any person claiming under them or through them in any way creating any kind of encumbrance over the suit schedule property. SCHEDULE PROPERTY All the piece and parcel of the house property bearing No.7, old No.842, 5th A Cross Road, BSK 1st Stage, 2nd Block, Bengaluru-560 050, measuring East-West: 40 feet and North-South: 39+41/2 consisting of Ground, first and second floors thereon and bounded on the:- EAST BY : Property No 841, C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 WEST BY : Property No.843, NORTH BY : Road & SOUTH BY : Property No.869.

The defendant No.1 has filed separate written- statement contending that the Will relied upon by the plaintiff dated 10.11.2010 has not at all been probated and therefore, the suit is not maintainable. The defendant No.1 has admitted that Sri T. Velayudhan had executed a gift deed in favour of the defendant No.2, but has denied the claim of ownership of the plaintiff on the basis of the Will C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 and the revenue documents obtained in her name. He has admitted that the plaintiff and the defendants were residing together during the lifetime of Sri T. Velayudhan, but has denied the request made by the plaintiff to quit and handover the possession. He has further admitted that he is in possession of the ground floor portion, excluding one room and the defendant No.2 is in possession of the 2 nd floor. It is further contended that the suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable and there is no landlord and tenant relationship between the plaintiff and the defendants No.1 and 2 and sought to dismiss the suit. The defendant No.2 has filed separate written- statement denying the execution of the Will relied upon by the plaintiff and has further stated that Sri T. Velayudhan during the year 2009-10 was not mentally stable and that Sri T. Velayudhan was finding difficult to identify even the family members and therefore, he could not have executed the alleged Will. It is further contended that in 2003 Sri T. C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 Velayudhan had requested the husband of defendant No.2 to develop the suit schedule property at his own costs and had permitted him to reap the benefits in the suit schedule property. The defendant No.2 has further stated that after the death of Sri Dorai Kannan, the plaintiff had no source of income and she had taken care of day to day expenses of the plaintiff. It is further contended that she had no obligation to allow the plaintiff to reside in the suit schedule property, however, she showed mercy on her. It is further contended that the plaintiff has relied on fabricated and created Will and the said Will could not have been executed in respect of ancestral properties in respect of Sri T. Velayudhan as he had no power to execute the Will. Hence, sought to dismiss the suit. The defendant no.3 was placed ex parte on 15.3.2019. Mahalakshmi V Alias Baby vs Sangeetha on 27 March, 2026

On the above pleadings of the parties, the following issues have been framed: C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 O.S.No. 647/2019 1) Whether the plaintiff proves that he is the lawful absolute owner of the suit schedule property on the basis of the Will dated 10.11.2010? 2) Whether the plaintiff proves that the defendants are total strangers to the schedule property and are not having any right over the same? 3) Whether plaintiff is entitled to the order of permanent injunction as he claimed? 4) Whether the defendants prove that the suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable? 5) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for any reliefs as sought for? 6) What decree or order? O.S.No. 4177/2020 Whether the plaintiff proves that suit schedule properties are the joint family properties and along with defendants is in joint possession? C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 Whether plaintiff is entitled for 1/3 share in suit schedule properties ? Whether plaintiff is entitled to declare Will dated 10.11.2010 is not binding on her 1/3 share? What decree or order?

In O.S.No. 4177/2020, the plaintiff, in order to prove her case, has got examined the GPA holder by name Sri S. Prasanna Kumar, who is none other than the son of the plaintiff, as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.9. On the other hand, the defendant No.4 examined herself as DW.1 and no documents are marked on their behalf. The defendants No.1 to 3 have not cross-examined the PW.1 and they have not led any independent evidence. Meanwhile in O.S.No. 647/2019, the plaintiff got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.15. The defendant No.2 has cross-examined the PW.1. The plaintiff has also examined one Smt. Adilakshmi, who C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 is the attesting witness to the Will as PW.2 and scribe as PW3. On the other hand, the defendant no.2 has examined her power of attorney holder as DW1 and got marked Ex.D1 to 13. Thereafter, the matter was posted for arguments. Vide order dtd 1.2.2025 this court has clubbed O.S.NO. 647/2019 with O.S.NO. 4177/2020 as the subject matter of the suits are same. Mahalakshmi V Alias Baby vs Sangeetha on 27 March, 2026 Heard both sides. Perused the records. My findings to the above issues are as under: IN O.S.No. 647/2019 Issue Nos.1 and 2 In the Affirmative Issue No.3 -- In the Negative Issue No.4 -- In the Negative Issue No.5 -- Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.6 -- As per the final order for the following: IN O.S.No. 4177/2020 Issue Nos.1 and 2 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 -- In the Negative C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 Issue No.4 -- As per the final order for the following: REASONS ISSUE Nos.1 TO 3 IN O.S.No.4177/2020:- These issues are interconnected and therefore, they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts.

The relationship between the parties is not in dispute. The plaintiff in O.S.No. 4177/2020 has sought the relief of partition and separate possession in item Nos.1 to 3 of the suit schedule properties to the extent of her 1/3rd share. Meanwhile, the plaintiff in O.S.No. 647/2019 has claimed the relief of declaration to declare that she is the absolute ownership of item No.2 of the plaint schedule property in O.S.No. 4177/2020, which is the only suit schedule property in O.S.No. 647/2019 and further to decare that the defendants are in the unauthorised C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 occupation of the suit property and to direct them to hand over the possession of the suit property. In the first place this court is required to examine the nature of the suit properties and their mode of acquisition by Velayuddan to ascertain the rival claims of the parties in O.S.NO.4177/2020 as the entire fulcrum of the case of the plaintiff in O.S.NO. 647/2019 is premised on the bequest made by Velayuddan in favour of her husband under the Will executed by Velayuddan on 10.11.2010 at Ex.P8 . COMPETENCY OF VELAYUDAN TO EXECUTE THE WILL IN RESPECT OF THE SUIT PROPERTIES: It is the specific claim of the plaintiff in O.S.NO. 4177/2020 C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 that item no.1 of the suit property in O.S.NO. 4177/2020 was inherited by the father of the plaintiff namely , Velayuddan and item no.2 was acquired by Velayuddan out of the joint family accruals and item no.3 is the exclusive property of the mother of the plaintiff acquired under the registered sale deed dtd 13.12.1971. No doubt the limitation for a suit for declaration is provided under Part III of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963. It is governed by Articles 56-58 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act. Under all the aforesaid three Articles, the limitation for a suit for declaration is three years from the date when the right to sue first accrues. It C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 is to be noted that when in a suit for declaration of title, a further relief is claimed in addition to mere declaration, the relief of declaration would only be an ancillary one and for the purposes of limitation, it would be governed by the relief that has been additionally claimed. The further relief claimed in the suit is for recovery of possession based upon title and as such its limitation would be 12 years in terms of Article 65 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act. 33 . In C. Mohammad Yunus vs. Syed Unnissa And Ors, AIR 1961 SC 808, it has been laid down that in a suit for declaration with a further relief, the limitation would be governed by the Article governing the suit for such further relief. In fact, a suit for a declaration of title to immovable property would not be barred so long as the right to such a property continues and subsists. When such right continues to subsist, the relief for declaration would be a continuing right and there would be no limitation for such C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 a suit. The principle is that the suit for a declaration for a right cannot be held to be barred so long as right to property subsists.

As such, in the instant case also in the absence of plea of adverse possession and the suit being filed within 12 years from the date of death of Velayudan the suit is in time. Thus the plaintiff has not only proved that she is the owner of the suit property in O.S.NO. 647/2019 but also proved that the defendants are the unauthorised occupants of the suit C/W O.S.No. 4177/2020 property and further she is entitled to recover the possession of the suit property from the defendants no.1 to 3 . In effect the plaintiff in O.S.NO. 647/2019 has also proved that the defendants are the strangers to the suit property and the defendants have failed to proved that the suit of the plaintiff the relief of declaration and injunction is not maintainable. However the claim of the plaintiff that she is entitled for the relief of permanent injunction to restrain the defendants from creating any kind of encumbrance over the suit property does not arise when the plaintiff herself has been declared as the absolute owner of the suit property . Therefore, issue no.1 , 2 & 5 are answered in the affirmative, issue no.3 does not arise for consideration and issue no.4 is answered in the negative.
